headline: Highest risk is medium: LangGraph can write shared state and broad-egress tools can amplify prompt injection, but Pathway is read-only/no-network so several pairwise harms are constrained.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can ingest developer-defined tool outputs and has shared state via checkpointer store; if Pathway output is fed into LangGraph as trusted content, instructions can be smuggled through the shared channel. Pathway itself has no direct input surfaces, so the risk hinges on orchestration, but the pair still has a plausible default pathway through shared state.
conditions: IF Pathway output is routed into LangGraph node prompts or state without provenance tags
IF the shared checkpointer store is readable by both agents
mitigations: Add provenance labels to all Pathway-derived fields before LangGraph consumes them
Separate checkpointer namespaces per agent run
Strip instruction-like text from Pathway outputs before passing to LangGraph
Require an allowlist for LangGraph tool-call arguments
requires-engineering: add content-security filtering at the orchestration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph can touch model-provider API keys and broad filesystem state, while Pathway is documented as having no filesystem or network egress. The pair does not show a direct shared workspace or outbound leak path from Pathway, so leakage is limited unless the orchestrator copies sensitive LangGraph state into Pathway inputs or logs.
conditions: IF LangGraph state containing secrets is written into a shared file or log that Pathway can read
IF the orchestrator forwards sensitive LangGraph context into Pathway processing
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared graph state
Disable verbose logging for LangGraph runs
Store Pathway inputs in a separate directory
Redact API keys before any handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries in the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has write_filesystem and execute_shell, while Pathway has no write, shell, or network capabilities. There is no direct overlap on mutable resources in the profiles, so conflict is only possible if the operator maps both onto the same external directory or mutable store; that is not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or database
IF the orchestrator grants Pathway write access not shown in its profile
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run Pathway read-only
Avoid concurrent writes from LangGraph to shared files
Use file locks for any shared artifact
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph can produce tool outputs and state that downstream nodes may treat as authoritative, and Pathway is a document-processing component that could consume those outputs. Because Pathway has no built-in verification surface in the profile, a bad LangGraph output can cascade into incorrect downstream processing unless the orchestrator adds checks.
conditions: IF Pathway consumes LangGraph-generated records without validation
IF LangGraph node outputs are used as source-of-truth inputs for Pathway
mitigations: Validate LangGraph outputs against a schema before handoff
Add checksum or signature checks on intermediate artifacts
Insert a human review step for high-impact records
Compare outputs against a second source
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but only LangGraph explicitly handles model-provider API keys and graph state; Pathway lists no data classes or residency constraints. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic logging/retention concerns rather than a proven breach pathway.
conditions: IF LangGraph graph state contains regulated data and is stored under a different retention policy than Pathway artifacts
IF deployment places EU PII into a non-compliant logging pipeline
mitigations: Document retention for shared artifacts
Exclude regulated data from graph state
Review logs for sensitive fields
Pin deployment region for any hosted components
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention
